points.display: The FIRE Act ensures that States are not penalized for wildfire mitigation practices like prescribed or controlled burns and brush clearing.
points.quote:
The FIRE Act ensures that States are not penalized for wildfire 
mitigation practices like prescribed or controlled burns and brush 
clearing.
points.speaker: Gary J. Palmer

points.display: Republicans are peddling this dangerous bill as an attempt to promote prescribed burns and combat wildfires. As has been true for the other dirty bills that we considered over the last week or so, this bill fails to address the stated goal and instead provides overly broad exemptions to the Clean Air Act that will harm American families and children.
points.quote:
Republicans are peddling this dangerous bill as an attempt to promote 
prescribed burns and combat wildfires. As has been true for the other 
dirty bills that we considered over the last week or so, this bill 
fails to address the stated goal and instead provides overly broad 
exemptions to the Clean Air Act that will harm American families and 
children.
points.speaker: Frank Pallone, Jr.

points.display: Crucially, this bill upholds strong environmental standards by stipulating that Federal requirements may only be waived if operators receive drilling permits and comply with historic preservation laws on the State level. Notably, the bill would not impact the royalties paid to the Federal Government. Therefore, it will not reduce the Federal revenues generated by geothermal production.
points.quote:
Crucially, this bill upholds strong environmental standards by 
stipulating that Federal requirements may only be waived if operators 
receive drilling permits and comply with historic preservation laws on 
the State level.
  Notably, the bill would not impact the royalties paid to the Federal 
Government. Therefore, it will not reduce the Federal revenues 
generated by geothermal production.
points.speaker: Bruce Westerman

points.display: The HEATS Act fixes that by cutting red tape and waiving Federal drilling permit requirements for geothermal wells on State and local lands. Operators will still go through a rigorous State-level permitting process, but they will no longer be subjected to duplicative Federal requirements that slow production, raise costs, and kill jobs.
points.quote:
The HEATS Act fixes that by cutting red tape and waiving Federal 
drilling permit requirements for geothermal wells on State and local 
lands. Operators will still go through a rigorous State-level 
permitting process, but they will no longer be subjected to duplicative 
Federal requirements that slow production, raise costs, and kill jobs.
points.speaker: Young Kim

points.display: Even good energy sources need good permitting policy. I am a strong supporter of geothermal energy, but the HEATS Act could undermine the on-the-ground support and good environmental track record geothermal currently enjoys.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, in closing, even good energy sources need good 
permitting policy. I am a strong supporter of geothermal energy, but 
the HEATS Act could undermine the on-the-ground support and good 
environmental track record geothermal currently enjoys.
points.speaker: Yassamin Ansari

points.display: While this may sound innocuous--oh, it is just subsurface; it is below what we can see with our eyes--without a Federal permit, the core safeguards for development affecting Federal resources would totally disappear. That includes protections under the National Environmental Policy Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, and the Endangered Species Act.
points.quote:
While this may sound innocuous--oh, it is just subsurface; it is 
below what we can see with our eyes--without a Federal permit, the core 
safeguards for development affecting Federal resources would totally 
disappear. That includes protections under the National Environmental 
Policy Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, and the Endangered 
Species Act.
points.speaker: Jared Huffman

points.display: I hear about trade. Trade is the Ways and Means Committee. I will say we did double foreign market development and market access program, which are tools to help our farmers get access to trade, but we don't have trade itself in our jurisdiction.
points.quote:
I hear about trade. Trade is the Ways and Means Committee. I will say 
we did double foreign market development and market access program, 
which are tools to help our farmers get access to trade, but we don't 
have trade itself in our jurisdiction.
points.speaker: Glenn Thompson

points.display: This bill will ensure that American farmers can continue to raise the food and fiber that ultimately finds its way into your home, and it will ensure that the next generation can continue that legacy. I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes'' with me on final passage, and I thank Chairman Thompson for bringing forth this bill today.
points.quote:
This bill will ensure that American farmers can continue to raise the 
food and fiber that ultimately finds its way into your home, and it 
will ensure that the next generation can continue that legacy.
  I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes'' with me on final passage, and I 
thank Chairman Thompson for bringing forth this bill today.
points.speaker: Frank D. Lucas

points.display: Democrats fought to fix that. We pushed for an additional $10 billion in support so these farmers could survive and compete. We were blocked.
points.quote:
Democrats fought to fix that. We pushed for an additional $10 billion 
in support so these farmers could survive and compete. We were blocked.
points.speaker: Jill N. Tokuda

points.display: As a result of this bill, more people will go hungry, more farmers will lose assistance to the conservation programs that are already oversubscribed, and more farmers who are struggling to make ends meet will find it more and more difficult to hang on to their farms.
points.quote:
As a 
result of this bill, more people will go hungry, more farmers will lose 
assistance to the conservation programs that are already 
oversubscribed, and more farmers who are struggling to make ends meet 
will find it more and more difficult to hang on to their farms.
points.speaker: Chellie Pingree

points.display: The underlying bill will allow for year-round sale of 15 percent ethanol and gasoline, which farmers say is needed to provide an additional market for their crops without impacting air quality.
points.quote:
The underlying bill will allow for year-round sale of 15 percent 
ethanol and gasoline, which farmers say is needed to provide an 
additional market for their crops without impacting air quality.
points.speaker: Brett Guthrie

points.display: E15 is homegrown American energy. Most importantly, eliminating the artificial prohibition on summer sales of E15 is an important step toward creating the consistent demand that will allow this industry to grow and stand on its own without RFS one day. We have to get this done first.
points.quote:
E15 is homegrown American energy. Most importantly, eliminating the 
artificial prohibition on summer sales of E15 is an important step 
toward creating the consistent demand that will allow this industry to 
grow and stand on its own without RFS one day.
  We have to get this done first.
points.speaker: Julie Fedorchak

points.display: This bill is disastrous for Wyoming refiners and independent petroleum producers, leading to a direct loss of at least 750 jobs in my home State.
points.quote:
This bill is disastrous for Wyoming refiners and independent 
petroleum producers, leading to a direct loss of at least 750 jobs in 
my home State.
points.speaker: Harriet M. Hageman

points.display: Expanding E15 is just the wrong direction to go. It is going to harm refiners. It is going to drive up the cost of gas.
points.quote:
Expanding E15 is just the wrong direction to go. 
It is going to harm refiners. It is going to drive up the cost of gas.
points.speaker: Chip Roy

points.display: It has been 250 years since we declared independence. As we celebrate this milestone, I think it is all the more worthy that we pass this bill and begin construction of the museum dedicated to the history of American women. Throughout our history, women have played a pivotal role in so many of our Nation's most celebrated achievements and innovations.
points.quote:
It has been 250 years 
since we declared independence. As we celebrate this milestone, I think 
it is all the more worthy that we pass this bill and begin construction 
of the museum dedicated to the history of American women.
  Throughout our history, women have played a pivotal role in so many 
of our Nation's most celebrated achievements and innovations.
points.speaker: Bryan Steil

points.display: I rise in opposition to this amended bill. I was a proud cosponsor of the bill, as introduced. Yet, instead of moving the bipartisan text, Republicans have hijacked this bill to give President Trump complete and total authority over the Smithsonian American Women's History Museum's location.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to this amended bill. I 
was a proud cosponsor of the bill, as introduced. Yet, instead of 
moving the bipartisan text, Republicans have hijacked this bill to give 
President Trump complete and total authority over the Smithsonian 
American Women's History Museum's location.
points.speaker: Mark Takano

points.display: This bill is about basic fairness and restoring a standard that respects both our veterans and the Constitution. Under current practice, a veteran who simply needs help managing their VA benefits can be reported to the FBI's background check system and lose their Second Amendment rights without ever appearing before a judge.
points.quote:
This bill is about basic fairness and restoring a standard that 
respects both our veterans and the Constitution. Under current 
practice, a veteran who simply needs help managing their VA benefits 
can be reported to the FBI's background check system and lose their 
Second Amendment rights without ever appearing before a judge.
points.speaker: Chuck Edwards

points.display: Every day, 17 veterans die by suicide, and 13 of them use a firearm to take their lives. That number is simply unacceptable to me, as I know it is to all of my colleagues, but I am deeply concerned that, with this bill, we are about to make it worse.
points.quote:
Every day, 17 veterans die by suicide, and 13 of them use a firearm 
to take their lives. That number is simply unacceptable to me, as I 
know it is to all of my colleagues, but I am deeply concerned that, 
with this bill, we are about to make it worse.
points.speaker: Debbie Wasserman Schultz

points.display: VA reported them not because they committed a crime or because a judge or a medical professional determined they were a danger to themselves or others. VA reported them to NICS simply because they needed help managing their benefits.
points.quote:
VA reported them not because they committed a crime or because a 
judge or a medical professional determined they were a danger to 
themselves or others. VA reported them to NICS simply because they 
needed help managing their benefits.
points.speaker: Mike Bost

points.display: While no silver bullet that will eradicate veteran suicide, making it easier for veterans suffering from severe mental illness or impairment to obtain a gun is not the answer. H.R. 1041 creates serious risks for a group of veterans who are already in a vulnerable position, and I cannot support it.
points.quote:
While no silver bullet that will eradicate veteran suicide, making it 
easier for veterans suffering from severe mental illness or impairment 
to obtain a gun is not the answer.
  H.R. 1041 creates serious risks for a group of veterans who are 
already in a vulnerable position, and I cannot support it.
points.speaker: Kelly Morrison

points.display: This legislation would provide the first meaningful increase in survivor benefits for families like Brileys since 1993. Over 500,000 survivors like Sharri receive Dependency and Indemnity Compensation from the VA.
points.quote:
This legislation would provide the first meaningful increase in 
survivor benefits for families like Brileys since 1993.
  Over 500,000 survivors like Sharri receive Dependency and Indemnity 
Compensation from the VA.
points.speaker: Mike Bost

points.display: Representative Barrett and House Republicans have engineered here an impossible choice. What they have said to the American people is that only by raising costs on one set of veterans can we afford to help another.
points.quote:
Representative Barrett and House Republicans have engineered here an 
impossible choice. What they have said to the American people is that 
only by raising costs on one set of veterans can we afford to help 
another.
points.speaker: Mark Takano

points.display: The CRACKDOWN Act would lower the threshold from 10 percent to 5 percent. If the State exceeds that level, we must take corrective action to improve program integrity.
points.quote:
The CRACKDOWN Act would lower the threshold from 10 percent to 5 
percent. If the State exceeds that level, we must take corrective 
action to improve program integrity.
points.speaker: Glenn Grothman

points.display: Our economy already loses an estimated $122 billion every year due to childcare shortages, and that is a policy failure. The bill before us does nothing to reduce childcare costs, increase supply, or improve conditions for providers, and it doesn't even reduce fraud.
points.quote:
Our economy already loses 
an estimated $122 billion every year due to childcare shortages, and 
that is a policy failure.
  The bill before us does nothing to reduce childcare costs, increase 
supply, or improve conditions for providers, and it doesn't even reduce 
fraud.
points.speaker: Robert C. "Bobby" Scott

points.display: For fiscal year 2027, the subcommittee's discretionary allocation is $26.27 billion, a $380 million, or 1.4 percent, decrease from fiscal year 2026 enacted levels. In a setting of $2 trillion deficits, these modest spending reductions are necessary.
points.quote:
For fiscal year 2027, the subcommittee's discretionary allocation is 
$26.27 billion, a $380 million, or 1.4 percent, decrease from fiscal 
year 2026 enacted levels.
  In a setting of $2 trillion deficits, these modest spending 
reductions are necessary.
points.speaker: Andy Harris

points.display: It makes substantial reductions across rural development, farm production and conservation, nutrition, and foreign aid programs. Most notably, House Republicans are proposing to drastically reduce fruit and vegetable benefits for 5 million low-income women, infants, and children in the WIC program.
points.quote:
It makes substantial 
reductions across rural development, farm production and conservation, 
nutrition, and foreign aid programs.
  Most notably, House Republicans are proposing to drastically reduce 
fruit and vegetable benefits for 5 million low-income women, infants, 
and children in the WIC program.
points.speaker: Sanford D. Bishop, Jr.

points.display: The question before this House is simple: Will we help Ukraine negotiate from a position of strength, or will we help Putin outlast American resolve? The Ukrainian people, our NATO allies, and the United States national security cannot afford to wait any longer for this body to act against Russia's brutal war in Ukraine.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, the question before this House is simple: 
Will we help Ukraine negotiate from a position of strength, or will we 
help Putin outlast American resolve?
  The Ukrainian people, our NATO allies, and the United States national 
security cannot afford to wait any longer for this body to act against 
Russia's brutal war in Ukraine.
points.speaker: Gregory W. Meeks

points.display: In the 2 years since we last approved a package, Ukrainians have endured two bitter winters of war. It is time for us to act. Russian drones have continued to rain terror on civilian neighborhoods.
points.quote:
In the 2 years since we last approved a package, 
Ukrainians have endured two bitter winters of war.
  It is time for us to act. Russian drones have continued to rain 
terror on civilian neighborhoods.
points.speaker: Steny H. Hoyer

points.display: It is important to recognize as we stand here today in the midst of a war with Iran, as the President is trying to secure an agreement that would require them not to pursue nuclear weapons, that the United States already has a commitment in an agreement with the then-third largest nuclear power, Ukraine.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, it is important to recognize as we stand 
here today in the midst of a war with Iran, as the President is trying 
to secure an agreement that would require them not to pursue nuclear 
weapons, that the United States already has a commitment in an 
agreement with the then-third largest nuclear power, Ukraine.
points.speaker: William R. Keating

points.display: I thank the gentleman for yielding, and I thank my colleagues on both sides of the aisle because there are not people on the floor of the House that support Putin.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I thank the gentleman for 
yielding, and I thank my colleagues on both sides of the aisle because 
there are not people on the floor of the House that support Putin.
points.speaker: J. French Hill

points.display: Let me start with a simple premise: What Russia did was terrible, and Vladimir Putin is a bad guy.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, let me start with a simple premise: What 
Russia did was terrible, and Vladimir Putin is a bad guy.
points.speaker: Randy Fine

points.display: I thank Chairman Mast for yielding time to speak on our national security and this critically important issue of supporting our partners and allies and deterring our adversaries.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I thank Chairman Mast for yielding time 
to speak on our national security and this critically important issue 
of supporting our partners and allies and deterring our adversaries.
points.speaker: Ryan Mackenzie

points.display: I rise in support of H.R. 5408, the Faster Labor Contracts Act, which ensures that workers can quickly and efficiently reach a first contract between a union and their employer.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 5408, the Faster Labor 
Contracts Act, which ensures that workers can quickly and efficiently 
reach a first contract between a union and their employer.
points.speaker: Robert C. "Bobby" Scott

points.display: I thank Mr. Scott for yielding. Mr. Speaker, when a union wins more fair pay and better working conditions for its members, it sets the bar higher for everyone.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I thank Mr. Scott for yielding.
  Mr. Speaker, when a union wins more fair pay and better working 
conditions for its members, it sets the bar higher for everyone.
points.speaker: Donald Norcross

points.display: I thank the distinguished ranking member for yielding. Mr. Speaker, I rise as a son of the labor movement and co-chair of the Congressional Labor Caucus in strong support of the Faster Labor Contracts Act.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I thank the distinguished ranking member 
for yielding.
  Mr. Speaker, I rise as a son of the labor movement and co-chair of 
the Congressional Labor Caucus in strong support of the Faster Labor 
Contracts Act.
points.speaker: Steven Horsford

points.display: I rise in opposition to H.R. 5408, the so-called Faster Labor Contracts Act.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to H.R. 5408, the so-called Faster 
Labor Contracts Act.
points.speaker: Tim Walberg

points.display: I thank the chairman for yielding the time. Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong opposition to H.R. 5408, the Faster Labor Contracts Act.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I thank the chairman for yielding the time.
  Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong opposition to H.R. 5408, the Faster 
Labor Contracts Act.
points.speaker: Rick W. Allen

points.display: I rise today in strong opposition to the so- called Faster Labor Contracts Act.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to the so-
called Faster Labor Contracts Act.
points.speaker: Randy Fine

points.display: I rise in strong support of H.R. 7892, the No Aid for Ghost Students Act of 2026, a simple and commonsense piece of legislation to fight fraud in our Federal student aid system.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of H.R. 7892, the No Aid for 
Ghost Students Act of 2026, a simple and commonsense piece of 
legislation to fight fraud in our Federal student aid system.
points.speaker: Tim Walberg

points.display: This is why the issue of fraud in our financial aid system is so pernicious.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, this is why the issue of fraud in our financial aid 
system is so pernicious.
points.speaker: Burgess Owens

points.display: I rise in opposition to H.R. 7892, the so-called No Aid for Ghost Students Act.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to H.R. 7892, the so-called No Aid 
for Ghost Students Act.
points.speaker: Robert C. "Bobby" Scott

points.display: I rise to oppose H.R. 7892, the so-called No Aid for Ghost Students Act.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise to oppose H.R. 7892, the so-called 
No Aid for Ghost Students Act.
points.speaker: Christian D. Menefee

points.display: The Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act dramatically enhances how agencies prevent fraud, especially during any future national emergency.
points.quote:
Madam Speaker, the Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act 
dramatically enhances how agencies prevent fraud, especially during any 
future national emergency.
points.speaker: James Comer

points.display: I am opposed to the Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act.
points.quote: I am opposed to the Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act.
points.speaker: James R. Walkinshaw

points.display: We are facing a national emergency of fraud in Federal programs that is impacting every American.
points.quote:
Madam Speaker, we are facing a national emergency of fraud in Federal 
programs that is impacting every American.
points.speaker: James Comer

points.display: I strongly support H.R. 8464, the Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act.
points.quote:
Madam Speaker, I strongly support H.R. 8464, the 
Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act.
points.speaker: Lauren Boebert

points.display: There is no doubt the Federal Government must do more to address this problem. That is why Oversight Committee Democrats have supported numerous antifraud measures, including the Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act, which seeks to add additional payment verification before checks are sent out the door.
points.quote:
There is no doubt the Federal Government must do more 
to address this problem.
  That is why Oversight Committee Democrats have supported numerous 
antifraud measures, including the Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and 
Treasury Data Access Act, which seeks to add additional payment 
verification before checks are sent out the door.
points.speaker: James R. Walkinshaw

points.display: No one in this Chamber disputes that improper and fraudulent payments are a serious problem. The question before us is not whether to fight fraud; it is how we fight fraud. If this bill actually does that--and I will give you a hint: It does not.
points.quote:
Madam Speaker, no one in this Chamber disputes that 
improper and fraudulent payments are a serious problem. The question 
before us is not whether to fight fraud; it is how we fight fraud.
  If this bill actually does that--and I will give you a hint: It does 
not.
points.speaker: Wesley Bell

points.display: FISA section 702 will expire on Friday. This bill extends the program until July 2.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, FISA section 702 will expire on Friday. This bill 
extends the program until July 2.
points.speaker: Jim Jordan

points.display: The Fourth Amendment protects the rights of all Americans. It does not have a ``unless it is just for another 3 weeks'' exception.
points.quote:
The 
Fourth Amendment protects the rights of all Americans. It does not have 
a ``unless it is just for another 3 weeks'' exception.
points.speaker: Jamie Raskin

points.display: This important legislation will finally end the outdated practice of changing our clocks twice a year and establish permanent daylight saving time.
points.quote:
This important legislation will finally end the 
outdated practice of changing our clocks twice a year and establish 
permanent daylight saving time.
points.speaker: Gus M. Bilirakis

points.display: Permanent time is a national decision with implications for every aspect of our health and economy. It deserves a robust, thoughtful debate and an amendment process that allows Members to test each provision of the bill.
points.quote:
Permanent time is a national decision with implications for every 
aspect of our health and economy. It deserves a robust, thoughtful 
debate and an amendment process that allows Members to test each 
provision of the bill.
points.speaker: Madeleine Dean

points.display: Financial privacy is fundamental to consumer trust and confidence in our financial system. As technology continues to transform financial services, protecting Americans' financial privacy remains an essential part of Congress' oversight role.
points.quote:
Financial privacy is fundamental to consumer trust and confidence in 
our financial system. As technology continues to transform financial 
services, protecting Americans' financial privacy remains an essential 
part of Congress' oversight role.
points.speaker: J. French Hill

points.display: I rise in opposition to H.R. 1181, a bill which makes it harder to catch criminals and makes our communities less safe.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to H.R. 1181, a bill which makes it 
harder to catch criminals and makes our communities less safe.
points.speaker: Mike Thompson

points.display: Financial institutions have already been using merchant codes to detect crimes like money laundering and human trafficking.
points.quote:
Financial institutions have already been using merchant codes to 
detect crimes like money laundering and human trafficking.
points.speaker: Maxwell Frost

points.display: My bill preserves two fundamental rights: the right to privacy and the right to bear arms. Americans should not be forced to disclose to payment processors when they buy firearms.
points.quote:
My bill 
preserves two fundamental rights: the right to privacy and the right to 
bear arms. Americans should not be forced to disclose to payment 
processors when they buy firearms.
points.speaker: Riley M. Moore

points.display: The bill maintains $1.8 billion for partners in the Indo-Pacific, including $500 million in military assistance for Taiwan. It provides unwavering support for Israel and fully funds the United States-Israel Memorandum of Understanding by providing $3.3 billion in security assistance.
points.quote:
The bill maintains $1.8 billion for partners in the Indo-Pacific, 
including $500 million in military assistance for Taiwan. It provides 
unwavering support for Israel and fully funds the United States-Israel 
Memorandum of Understanding by providing $3.3 billion in security 
assistance.
points.speaker: Mario Diaz-Balart

points.display: Sadly, this bill has zero for Ukraine, our ally fighting the Russian invader. That is a grave mistake and absolutely the wrong approach. It is a dangerous signal at a time when we ought to show unwavering support for Ukraine's defense of its homeland.
points.quote:
Sadly, this bill has zero for Ukraine, our ally fighting the Russian 
invader. That is a grave mistake and absolutely the wrong approach. It 
is a dangerous signal at a time when we ought to show unwavering 
support for Ukraine's defense of its homeland.
points.speaker: Steny H. Hoyer

points.display: Less competition means fewer financing options, higher borrowing costs, and less investment on Main Street, not Wall Street, as some of my colleagues are trying to assert. This bill lowers unnecessary regulatory costs for community and midsize banks, not those big business center banks on Wall Street and in New York and around the world.
points.quote:
Less competition means fewer financing options, higher 
borrowing costs, and less investment on Main Street, not Wall Street, 
as some of my colleagues are trying to assert.
  This bill lowers unnecessary regulatory costs for community and 
midsize banks, not those big business center banks on Wall Street and 
in New York and around the world.
points.speaker: Bill Huizenga

points.display: Now, this bill will actually make it easier for more, not less consolidation. The bill is bad for new banks but great for megabanks.
points.quote:
Now, this bill will actually make it easier for more, not less 
consolidation. The bill is bad for new banks but great for megabanks.
points.speaker: Maxine Waters

points.display: This Congress has a constitutional duty to fund the government. If Article I teaches us anything, it is that governing means doing the work, not waiting for a crisis. It is a responsibility I have never viewed as optional and one I have remained committed to honoring through regular order.
points.quote:
This Congress has a constitutional duty to fund the government. If 
Article I teaches us anything, it is that governing means doing the 
work, not waiting for a crisis. It is a responsibility I have never 
viewed as optional and one I have remained committed to honoring 
through regular order.
points.speaker: Tom Cole

points.display: Unfortunately, it seems increasingly likely that, at some point, a continuing resolution will be necessary. That does not mean we must rush through an incomplete, hastily constructed, one-sided stopgap measure that fails to adequately meet the government's funding needs.
points.quote:
Unfortunately, it seems increasingly likely that, at some point, a 
continuing resolution will be necessary. That does not mean we must 
rush through an incomplete, hastily constructed, one-sided stopgap 
measure that fails to adequately meet the government's funding needs.
points.speaker: Rosa L. DeLauro

points.display: Today, I have the opportunity to speak briefly with regards to the fiscal year 2027 NDAA. The bipartisan bill that passed out of committee includes many quality-of-life provisions and priorities for our servicemembers and their families.
points.quote:
Mr. Chair, today, I have the opportunity to speak briefly with 
regards to the fiscal year 2027 NDAA.
  The bipartisan bill that passed out of committee includes many 
quality-of-life provisions and priorities for our servicemembers and 
their families.
points.speaker: Chrissy Houlahan

points.display: The FY27 NDAA takes several steps to ensure that our servicemembers operate with unmatched capabilities to deter and defeat any adversaries. This bill allows the Secretary of War to enter into multiyear procurement contracts for both the F-15EX and F-35 aircraft. H.R. 8800 prioritizes helicopter and rotorcraft procurement, authorizing the purchase of additional Chinook, Black Hawk, and Grey Wolf helicopters.
points.quote:
The FY27 NDAA takes several steps to ensure that our servicemembers 
operate with unmatched capabilities to deter and defeat any 
adversaries.
  This bill allows the Secretary of War to enter into multiyear 
procurement contracts for both the F-15EX and F-35 aircraft.
  H.R. 8800 prioritizes helicopter and rotorcraft procurement, 
authorizing the purchase of additional Chinook, Black Hawk, and Grey 
Wolf helicopters.
points.speaker: Robert J. Wittman

points.display: I believe that Members of Congress should serve the public, not profit from public office. That is why I strongly support the Stop Insider Trading Act, which would prohibit Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I believe that Members of Congress should 
serve the public, not profit from public office.
  That is why I strongly support the Stop Insider Trading Act, which 
would prohibit Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent 
children from purchasing individual stocks.
points.speaker: Thomas H. Kean, Jr.

points.display: This bill would throw our elections into chaos, the effective date being October 20 of 2026, 90 days from today, right in the middle of this midterm election. In 90 days, tens of millions of Americans will have already cast their ballots by person and by mail. This bill would upend the November midterms, and that is exactly the point.
points.quote:
This bill would throw our elections into chaos, the effective date 
being October 20 of 2026, 90 days from today, right in the middle of 
this midterm election. In 90 days, tens of millions of Americans will 
have already cast their ballots by person and by mail. This bill would 
upend the November midterms, and that is exactly the point.
points.speaker: Joseph D. Morelle

points.display: I rise in support of H.R. 8884, the Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act, introduced by our colleague from Georgia, Representative Austin Scott.
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 8884, the Removing Barriers to 
Work for Disabled Americans Act, introduced by our colleague from
